using MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests;
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Testing;
edits.replace: using MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests;

If the type carries neither `[MessagePackObject]` nor `[DataContract]`, the formatter serializes it in *contractless* mode: every public, read-write instance property and field is serialized under its name as a string key.
Read-only members are skipped because they cannot be deserialized.

If the type does carry `[MessagePackObject]` or `[DataContract]`, those attributes are honoured just as they are for types in your own project:
`[Key]` and `[IgnoreMember]` (or `[DataMember]` and `[IgnoreDataMember]`) on its members decide the keys and which members are serialized.
`[DataContract]` is part of the base class library, so a dependency-free library can use it without referencing MessagePack.

```cs
// In ProjectA, which does not reference MessagePack:
[DataContract]
public class MyObject
{
    [DataMember(Order = 0)]
    public int Id { get; set; }

    [DataMember(Order = 1)]
    public string Label { get; set; }

    public string Secret { get; set; } // not serialized
}
```

All keys of a type must be integers or all must be strings, and every serialized member must be public and read-write.
